subject: Acceptance window change: priority ladder, MAP updates, and escalation brief
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Acceptance window — procurement delay; proposed priority ladder and MAP update

Team,

Quick summary: Nova Clinic signaled this morning that procurement/legal review will push their acceptance sign-off out by at least three weeks. They flagged an internal vendor validation packet that wasn't in our original MAP and will take time to assemble.

Impact: if acceptance slips, go-live window moves and we risk feature gating in their pilot. I want a short, pragmatic plan we can share with the customer that:
- preserves the current sprint for engineering validation (staggered validation),
- narrows the acceptance items we need for initial sign-off (priority ladder), and
- sets an escalation path if procurement exceeds the new target date.

Please review the attached MAP_v3.xlsx and the risk_register_20261203.csv. Ask: Ben, can you draft the customer-facing note and priority ladder? Jordan, map which deliverables (by engineering sprint) we can frontload for a technical validation window. Marissa, please prepare an exec note if we need to elevate to Jonas for discount/credit approval.

Target: I want Ben's draft by EOD today so we can align and send to Alice no later than Monday.

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance window — procurement delay; proposed priority ladder and MAP update

Thanks Rachel — I reviewed the MAP and risk register. Draft notes:

1) Priority ladder (short):
   - Phase 1 (Tech validation): API endpoints, sample inference latency, data handling contract.
   - Phase 2 (Pilot acceptance): subset of supervised evaluation cases + security attestation summary.
   - Phase 3 (Full acceptance): all MAP items + SOC evidence.

2) Proposed dates:
   - Tech validation window: Dec 14–18 (one-week sandbox access)
   - Acceptance target (re-baseline): Jan 10 (contingent on legal packet)

3) Escalation ladder: procurement slow → Marissa engages finance for credit discussion → Jonas for SLA/contract exceptions.

I'm attaching a clean PDF (Proposed_MAP_v3.pdf) to share with Alice and a trimmed MAP_v3.xlsx for our internal priories. If nobody objects I'll send the customer note Monday morning.

Ben
Ben Carter
Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference
(attachment: MAP_v3.xlsx, risk_register_20261203.csv, Proposed_MAP_v3.pdf)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@novaclinic.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-08T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Proposal: staged acceptance + priority ladder for RDW-2987

Alice —

Thanks again for the call on Tuesday. To make this concrete and reduce blocker risk on your side, we've put together a proposed staged acceptance path and a short priority ladder that narrows the initial acceptance criteria to the most time-sensitive items.

Key points:
- Tech validation window: we can open a sandbox for your engineers Dec 14–18 so your team can perform the API/connectivity checks and initial inference verification. This requires minimal procurement paperwork.
- Re-baselined acceptance date: given your legal/procurement timing, our proposed new target is Jan 10. If you can confirm receipt of the required vendor validation packet by Dec 20 we can hold to that date.
- Priority ladder: we suggest signing off Phase 1 (Tech validation) first, then Phase 2 (Pilot acceptance) once the legal attestation is delivered.
- Escalation: if procurement extends beyond Jan 10 we recommend a short, scoped contract addendum; Marissa from finance is available to discuss credit/term accommodations.

Attached: Proposed_MAP_v3.pdf (high level) and a trimmed checklist. Please let us know whether Dec 14–18 works for your engineers and whether procurement can aim to deliver the vendor packet by Dec 20. If you prefer a quick sync, I can schedule 30 minutes tomorrow.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@novaclinic.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nova Clinic Procurement <procurement@novaclinic.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T15:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: staged acceptance + priority ladder for RDW-2987

Rachel —

Appreciate the clear plan. Procurement/legal are stretched this quarter and the vendor validation packet is still being compiled (we expect to complete by Dec 22–23, not Dec 20). The sandbox window Dec 14–18 is tight for our lead engineers — they have site audits that week.

Two asks:
1) Can we shift the sandbox window to Dec 21–23 for a short warm-up?
2) If we can't complete the vendor packet until Dec 23, can we push the re-baseline target to Jan 17? We still want to progress the pilot but need realistic dates.

I'll schedule a 20-minute touch tomorrow to align.

Thanks,
Alice Gomez
Head of Engineering, Nova Clinic
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-19T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Escalation brief: Nova Clinic procurement slip — recommendation and approval asks

Jonas / Rachel —

Recap: Nova Clinic pushed vendor packet completion to Dec 23 and requested the sandbox be moved to Dec 21–23. They proposed Jan 17 as the re-baselined acceptance date. The customer remains engaged; this is not a lost deal but a schedule slip driven by external audit/resource constraints.

Recommendation:
- Approve the sandbox shift to Dec 21–23.
- Accept the re-baseline to Jan 17 conditional on receiving the vendor packet by Dec 23.
- Approve a contingency credit of up to 5% (pro-rated) if acceptance slips further beyond Jan 31 — this will be used as leverage to keep their pilot moving and covers potential revenue exposure. Marissa/Finance will own the credit mechanics if approved.

Rationale: this preserves the customer relationship and keeps the tech validation momentum. Worst-case cost of the 5% credit is lower than lost rollout and multi-quarter delays.

For approval: Jonas — please confirm whether you approve the contingency credit and the re-baseline conditionality. If approved, we'll finalize the addendum and send to Nova's procurement.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
